The live read at 0x013eb250 shows the four bytes at 0x013eb258 are ff ff 7f 7f, i.e. the little-endian dword 0x7f7fffff, which is the IEEE-754 single-precision bit pattern for FLT_MAX
The live read at 0x013eb8b0 shows sixteen bytes 00 00 00 80 repeated four times, i.e. four lanes of 0x80000000 - a pure sign mask with no magnitude bits, so XORPS can only flip signs

callers_evidence_note: The briefing lists 22 callers; the live scan found 28 code references. The four inspected sites are given above; the remaining 24 are listed as a group and are not characterised.
semantic_contract: The function initialises a 24-byte object in place and returns nothing. It writes six consecutive floats: the first three at offsets +0x00, +0x04 and +0x08 receive the float constant stored at 0x013eb258, whose bit pattern read live is 0x7F7FFFFF, i.e. +FLT_MAX; the last three at +0x0C, +0x10 and +0x14 receive that same constant XORed with the 16-byte sign mask at 0x013eb8b0, i.e. -FLT_MAX. It reads nothing from the destination, so it is idempotent and safe on uninitialised storage, it calls nothing, it touches no other memory and it has no branch. The resulting object has a lower bound above its upper bound on every axis, which is the inverted or empty state that a union or intersection accumulator must start from in order for the first real operand to replace it entirely.
classification_rationale: The complete 49-instruction body, the frame, the six destination offsets, both global constants with their live-read values, the single 0x0C bias instruction and the absence of any branch, callee or destination read are all established directly from the disassembly and from live memory reads, and the resulting state - a lower bound above the upper bound on all three axes - pins the semantics as the identity element of a bounding-volume accumulator rather than leaving it to interpretation. The type identification is an SDK correspondence, but it is corroborated by a layout that is hard to explain any other way: a 24-byte object whose second vector starts at the unaligned offset 0x0C is two consecutive 12-byte vectors and nothing else, and the SDK's own comment records the same default-construct-then-pass-as-out-parameter callsite pattern. The one divergence found - the SDK declaring -1/+1 where the binary stores FLT_MAX and -FLT_MAX - is a defect in the SDK's inline body, is recorded, and does not weaken the reconstruction of the binary.
semantic_findings: Both constants were read out of the image rather than inferred: 0x013eb258 holds the bytes ff ff 7f 7f and 0x013eb8b0 holds four lanes of 0x80000000.

The second group is produced by XORPS against a sign-only mask and consumed by MOVSS, so each of the three negations is a single sign-bit flip; the 16-byte width of the mask is an SSE artefact and not a wider operation.
The function reads nothing from its destination, so it is idempotent and needs no initialised storage - a property the reconstruction preserves and the model test checks by running it twice.
The 0x0C bias at 0x00409cbf is the only instruction that establishes where the second group starts, and it is what identifies the object as two consecutive 12-byte vectors.
The state it writes, lower above upper on every axis, is the identity for a union or intersection, and the callsites use it that way: construct, then hand the object to an out-parameter helper.
0x004ad550 constructs the same object twice in a row, which is only meaningful because the constructor does not read the old contents.
The body is entirely SSE with no x87 and no MMX state, so it has no hidden floating-point register obligation.
unresolved_questions: Is the type really Math::BoundingBox? The 24-byte size and the 0x0C second-vector offset match the SDK declaration exactly, but any other 24-byte aggregate of two unaligned 12-byte vectors would match equally well, and the binary names it nowhere.

Why is the constructor out of line? Six constant stores would normally be inlined; the 28 direct callsites and 0 vtable references argue against a virtual override, so an unoptimised translation unit or an address taken somewhere is the likely explanation, and neither was checked.
Do all 24 uninspected callsites pass the result as an out-parameter, or do some keep it as a member? The four inspected ones all do.
Is the inverted state read back anywhere as a sentinel - for example a containment test that relies on it - or is it only ever an initial value? No reader was identified.

The neighbouring constants at 0x013eb254 (00 00 80 00) and 0x013eb260 (ff ff ff 7f) were read while locating the real one and are recorded as context only. Whether they belong to the same table of float constants, and what else references them, was not investigated.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has been captured. Whether any of the 28 callsites actually passes the constructed object on to a union or intersection without overwriting it first is a runtime fact.
Runtime patching of either global constant cannot be excluded statically; both were read from the on-disk image only.
